body.statement: For every \(n\ge2\), the construction \(\mathfrak H_n^{\mathrm{comp}}\) yields deterministic numbers \(0<\ell\le h\le1\), amplitudes \(a,b>0\), and two finite priors \(\Pi_+\) and \(\Pi_-\), supported on \(\mathcal P(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\), under each of which \(\tau_P(0)\) is constant, such that their constants differ by at least \(c\rho_n\) and the genuine fixed-\(n\) observed-data product mixtures have squared Hellinger distance at most \(1/4\).  More precisely, the singleton conditional sign-mixture laws are equal; if \(Q_{r,+}\) and \(Q_{r,-}\) denote the two conditional sign-mixture laws on any dependency component of size \(r\ge2\), then \[H^2(Q_{r,+},Q_{r,-})\le Ca^2b^2r^4(9/2)^r,\] and the full mixtures satisfy \[H^2\!\left(\int P_O^{\otimes n}\,d\Pi_+,\int P_O^{\otimes n}\,d\Pi_-\right)\le Cn^2h^d\ell^da^2b^2\le\frac14.\]  The construction keeps \(P_X\) exactly uniform on the full cube and uses neither an occupancy conditioning event nor Poissonization.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(p=3/8\).  We give the construction and prove every asserted property for the actual fixed-\(n\) experiment.

Define \(u(t)=e^{-1/t}\mathbf1\{t>0\}\),
\[
\chi(t)=\frac{u(1-t)}{u(1-t)+u(t-1/2)},
\qquad f(z)=\prod_{k=1}^d\chi(z_k).
\]
The denominator is positive for every \(t\), and direct differentiation at the flat endpoints shows that \(u\), hence \(\chi\) and \(f\), is \(C^\infty\).  Moreover, \(0\le f\le1\), \(f(0)=1\), and \(f(z)=0\) if any \(z_k\ge1\).  Likewise set
\[
\zeta(t)=e^{-1/(1-t^2)}\mathbf1\{|t|<1\}.
\]
This is a nonnegative \(C^\infty\) function supported on \([-1,1]\) and is bounded below by a positive constant on \([-1/2,1/2]\).

For \(0<\ell\le1\), let
\[
J_\ell=\{j\in\mathbb Z^d:\operatorname{dist}_\infty(\ell j,D_0)\le\ell\},
\quad
\phi_j(x)=\prod_{k=1}^d\zeta(x_k/\ell-j_k),
\quad
A_\ell(x)=\sum_{j\in J_\ell}\phi_j(x)^2,
\quad
\psi_j(x)=\frac{\phi_j(x)}{\sqrt{A_\ell(x)}}.
\]
The set \(J_\ell\) is finite.  For every \(x\in D_0\), coordinatewise nearest-integer rounding supplies \(j\in J_\ell\) with \(\|x/\ell-j\|_\infty\le1/2\).  Thus \(A_\ell\ge c_d>0\) on a neighborhood of \(D_0\).  At most \(3^d\) functions \(\phi_j\) are nonzero at a point.  The product and chain rules, applied inductively to \(A_\ell^{-1/2}\), therefore give, for every multi-index \(\nu\),
\[
\sum_j\psi_j(x)^2=1,\qquad
\operatorname{supp}(\psi_j)\subseteq\{x:\|x-\ell j\|_\infty\le\ell\},
\qquad
\|D^\nu\psi_j\|_\infty\le C_\nu\ell^{-|\nu|}. \tag{18}
\]
In particular, for independent Rademacher signs \(\vartheta=(\vartheta_j:j\in J_\ell)\),
\[
\left|\sum_j\vartheta_j\psi_j(x)\right|
\le \sqrt{3^d}\left(\sum_j\psi_j(x)^2\right)^{1/2}=:B. \tag{19}
\]

For \(0<\ell\le h\le1\), define
\[
f_h(x)=f(x/h),\qquad
F_\vartheta(x)=f_h(x)\sum_j\vartheta_j\psi_j(x),
\qquad K_h(x)=f_h(x)^2.
\]
Independence and centering of the signs and (18) imply, pointwise,
\[
\mathbb E_\vartheta F_\vartheta(x)=0,\qquad
\mathbb E_\vartheta F_\vartheta(x)^2=K_h(x),\qquad
|F_\vartheta(x)|\le B,\qquad 0\le K_h(x)\le1. \tag{20}
\]
For any fixed \(s>0\), put \(m=\lceil s\rceil-1\).  Product differentiation, (18), and \(\ell\le h\) bound every derivative through order \(m+1\) of \(F_\vartheta\) by \(C\ell^{-|\nu|}\), uniformly in \(\vartheta\), and every such derivative of \(K_h\) by \(Ch^{-|\nu|}\).  If \(D^mG\) denotes an order-\(m\) derivative, then
\[
|D^mG(x)-D^mG(y)|
\le C r^{-m}\min\{1,\|x-y\|_\infty/r\}
\le C r^{-s}\|x-y\|_\infty^{s-m}, \tag{21}
\]
with \(r=\ell\) for \(G=F_\vartheta\) and \(r=h\) for \(G=K_h\).  The first inequality uses respectively the sup-norm and the mean-value bound, and the second follows by splitting at \(\|x-y\|_\infty=r\).  It also covers integral \(s\), because then \(s-m=1\).  Consequently
\[
\|F_\vartheta\|_{\mathcal H_d^s(1)}\le C_s\ell^{-s},
\qquad
\|K_h\|_{\mathcal H_d^s(1)}\le C_sh^{-s}, \tag{22}
\]
where the notation in (22) means that every defining derivative bound and seminorm is bounded by the displayed right-hand side.

Choose fixed positive constants \(a_0,b_0\) so small that
\[
a_0B\le1/16,\qquad b_0\{B+a_0/p\}\le1/8. \tag{23}
\]
For amplitudes \(0<a\le a_0\), \(0<b\le b_0\), \(\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}\), and \(\vartheta\in\{-1,1\}^{J_\ell}\), define
\[
\begin{split}
e_\vartheta(x)&=p+aF_\vartheta(x),\\
\mu_{0,\varepsilon,\vartheta}(x)&=\frac12+\varepsilon bF_\vartheta(x)
+\frac{\varepsilon ab}{1-p}K_h(x),\\
\tau_\varepsilon(x)&=-\frac{\varepsilon ab}{p(1-p)}K_h(x),\\
\mu_{1,\varepsilon,\vartheta}(x)&=\frac12+\varepsilon bF_\vartheta(x)
-\frac{\varepsilon ab}{p}K_h(x).
\end{split} \tag{24}
\]
The last three lines satisfy \(\mu_{1,\varepsilon,\vartheta}-\mu_{0,\varepsilon,\vartheta}=\tau_\varepsilon\).  By (19) and (23), \(e_\vartheta\in[5/16,7/16]\) and both response means lie in \([3/8,5/8]\).

We now choose the deterministic scales.  With \(S=\alpha+\beta\), let
\[
\ell=c_\ell n^{-\eta/S},\qquad h=\ell^{S/\gamma},
\qquad a=c_a\ell^\alpha,\qquad b=c_b\ell^\beta, \tag{25}
\]
where \(0<c_\ell\le1\), \(0<c_a\le a_0\), and \(0<c_b\le b_0\) will be fixed below.  Since \(S<S_\star<\gamma\), \(0<\ell\le h\le1\).  Equations (22) and (25) show that the \(\alpha\)-H\"older size of \(4aF_\vartheta\) is at most \(Cc_a\), the \(\beta\)-H\"older size of \(bF_\vartheta\) is at most \(Cc_b\), and
\[
ab\|K_h\|_{\mathcal H_d^\beta(1)}
\le Cc_ac_b\ell^{S(1-\beta/\gamma)}\le Cc_ac_b,
\qquad
ab\|K_h\|_{\mathcal H_d^\gamma(1)}\le Cc_ac_b. \tag{26}
\]
Here \(\gamma>\beta\) is used in the first inequality.  Starting from the constants \(4p=3/2\) and \(1/2\), and then decreasing \(c_a,c_b\), (23), (26), and \(L\ge4\) prove
\[
4e_\vartheta\in\mathcal H_d^\alpha(L),\quad 1\le4e_\vartheta\le2,\quad
\mu_{0,\varepsilon,\vartheta}\in\mathcal H_d^\beta(L),\quad
\tau_\varepsilon\in\mathcal H_d^\gamma(L),\quad
1/8\le\mu_{a,\varepsilon,\vartheta}\le7/8. \tag{27}
\]

For each pair \((\varepsilon,\vartheta)\), construct a full-data law as follows.  Draw \(X\) uniformly on \(D_0\); conditional on \(X=x\), draw \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) independently with the two Bernoulli means in (24), draw \(A\) independently of them with success probability \(e_\vartheta(x)\), and set \(Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\).  This law satisfies consistency and conditional exchangeability by construction, and all remaining member conditions of \(\mathrm{def:exact\mbox{-}model}\) follow from (24) and (27).  Thus every constructed law belongs to \(\mathcal P(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\).  Let \(\Pi_\varepsilon\) be the uniform prior on the finite set of these laws as \(\vartheta\) varies.  Since \(f_h(0)=K_h(0)=1\), its target is constant over the prior and equals
\[
\tau_\varepsilon(0)=-\frac{\varepsilon ab}{p(1-p)}. \tag{28}
\]

It remains to control the full product mixtures.  At a fixed \(x\), abbreviate \(F=F_\vartheta(x)\) and \(K=K_h(x)\).  For real \((s,t)\), replace \((a,\varepsilon b)\) in (24) by \((s,t)\).  In the cell order \((A,Y)=(1,1),(1,0),(0,1),(0,0)\), the four probabilities are
\[
\begin{split}
q_{11}(s,t)&=p/2+sF/2+ptF+st(F^2-K)-s^2tKF/p,\\
q_{10}(s,t)&=p/2+sF/2-ptF-st(F^2-K)+s^2tKF/p,\\
q_{01}(s,t)&=(1-p)/2-sF/2+(1-p)tF-st(F^2-K)-s^2tKF/(1-p),\\
q_{00}(s,t)&=(1-p)/2-sF/2-(1-p)tF+st(F^2-K)+s^2tKF/(1-p).
\end{split} \tag{29}
\]
Their sum is one.  By (20), for each cell \(z\),
\[
\mathbb E_\vartheta q_z(s,t;x)=q_{0,z},
\qquad q_0=(p/2,p/2,(1-p)/2,(1-p)/2). \tag{30}
\]
Thus the singleton conditional mixtures under \(t=b\) and \(t=-b\) are not merely close: both equal \(q_0\).

After decreasing \(a_0,b_0\) if necessary, (19), (23), and the generative form (24) ensure, throughout \(|s|\le a_0\), \(|t|\le b_0\),
\[
\frac12\le \frac{q_z(s,t;x)}{q_{0,z}}\le\frac32. \tag{31}
\]
Indeed, treatment probabilities then lie in \([5/16,7/16]\) and response means in \([3/8,5/8]\); direct comparison with \(q_0\) gives (31).  Formula (29), together with \(|F|\le B\) and \(0\le K\le1\), also bounds the first \(s\)-derivative, first \(t\)-derivative, and mixed \((s,t)\)-derivative of every ratio in (31) by a constant \(C_0\).

Fix arbitrary locations \(x_1,\ldots,x_r\) whose active sign sets may overlap, and a cell vector \(z=(z_1,\ldots,z_r)\).  Relative to \(q_0^{\otimes r}\), the conditional mixture likelihood is
\[
M_r(s,t;z)=\mathbb E_\vartheta\prod_{i=1}^r
\frac{q_{z_i}(s,t;x_i)}{q_{0,z_i}}.
\]
The expectation is a finite sum.  Differentiating it, the product rule gives \(r\) terms in which both derivatives hit one factor and \(r(r-1)\) terms in which they hit two factors.  By (31) and the derivative bounds,
\[
|\partial_s\partial_tM_r(s,t;z)|\le C_1r^2(3/2)^r. \tag{32}
\]
At \(s=0\), replacing every sign \(\vartheta_j\) by \(-\vartheta_j\) replaces \(F_\vartheta\) by \(-F_\vartheta\) without changing its prior law.  Inspection of (29) gives \(M_r(0,b;z)=M_r(0,-b;z)\).  Two applications of the fundamental theorem of calculus and (32) yield
\[
|M_r(a,b;z)-M_r(a,-b;z)|
\le\int_0^a\int_{-b}^b|\partial_s\partial_tM_r(s,t;z)|\,dt\,ds
\le2C_1abr^2(3/2)^r. \tag{33}
\]
Both likelihoods in (33) are at least \(2^{-r}\) by (31).  Therefore
\[
\begin{split}
H^2(Q_{r,+},Q_{r,-})
&=\sum_zq_0^{\otimes r}(z)
\frac{|M_r(a,b;z)-M_r(a,-b;z)|^2}
{\{\sqrt{M_r(a,b;z)}+\sqrt{M_r(a,-b;z)}\}^2}\\
&\le Ca^2b^2r^4(9/2)^r. 
\end{split} \tag{34}
\]
For \(r=1\), (30) gives equality of the two laws and hence zero distance.

Condition now on the actual fixed vector \(X_{1:n}\).  Retain indices with \(f_h(X_i)\ne0\), and join \(i\) and \(j\) when \(\|X_i-X_j\|_\infty\le2\ell\).  If one sign \(\vartheta_k\) occurs in both \(F_\vartheta(X_i)\) and \(F_\vartheta(X_j)\), (18) implies this edge relation.  Hence distinct connected components depend on disjoint sets of independent signs.  Inactive observations have \(F_\vartheta=K_h=0\), and so have exactly the baseline cell law.  It follows, for the actual shared-sign prior, that the conditional product mixture factors over the graph components.

For probability laws \(P_j,Q_j\), their Hellinger affinities multiply under products.  Since \(H^2(P,Q)=2-2\int\sqrt{dP\,dQ}\), the elementary inequality \(1-\prod_jx_j\le\sum_j(1-x_j)\), \(0\le x_j\le1\), proves
\[
H^2\!\left(\bigotimes_jP_j,\bigotimes_jQ_j\right)
\le\sum_jH^2(P_j,Q_j). \tag{35}
\]
Let \(N_r\) be the number of graph components of size \(r\).  By (34)--(35), the conditional squared distance is at most
\[
Ca^2b^2\sum_{r=2}^nr^4(9/2)^rN_r. \tag{36}
\]

A component of size \(r\) is a connected labeled subset.  A connected graph contains a spanning tree.  Repeatedly delete the least-labeled leaf of a labeled tree and record its neighbor; the resulting word has length \(r-2\) over an alphabet of size \(r\).  Conversely, the multiplicity of each label in the word determines its current degree minus one, so repeatedly adjoining the least absent label reconstructs the unique deleted leaf and its incident edge.  This proves directly that there are \(r^{r-2}\) labeled trees.  For each such tree, integrate a root over the active set, which is contained in \([0,h]^d\), and then integrate every child over a sup-norm ball of radius \(2\ell\) about its parent.  Uniform independent design therefore gives
\[
\mathbb E N_r\le \binom nr r^{r-2}h^d(4\ell)^{d(r-1)}. \tag{37}
\]
No occupancy event has been imposed in (37).  Furthermore,
\[
\log(r!)=\sum_{k=1}^r\log k\ge\int_1^r\log x\,dx
=r\log r-r+1,
\]
so \(r!\ge(r/e)^r\).  With \(A=9/2\), (37) implies
\[
\mathbb E\sum_{r=2}^nr^4A^rN_r
\le nh^d\sum_{r=2}^nr^2(eA)^r(4^dn\ell^d)^{r-1}. \tag{38}
\]
If \(eA4^dn\ell^d\le1/2\), the series in (38) is at most \(Cn\ell^d\): factor out its first power of \(4^dn\ell^d\) and sum \(\sum_{r\ge2}r^2 2^{-(r-1)}<\infty\).  Hence (36)--(38) give
\[
\mathbb E_XH^2\{\mathsf M_+(\,\cdot\mid X_{1:n}),
\mathsf M_-(\,\cdot\mid X_{1:n})\}
\le Cn^2h^d\ell^da^2b^2. \tag{39}
\]
The two mixtures have the same uniform \(X_{1:n}\)-marginal.  Expanding the defining Hellinger integral therefore shows that their unconditional squared Hellinger distance is exactly the left side of (39).  This proves the requested fixed-\(n\) inequality directly, without Poissonization.

It remains only to fix the constants simultaneously.  From the definition of \(\eta\),
\[
1-\frac{d\eta}{S}<0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
S<\frac{d\gamma}{2\gamma+d}, \tag{40}
\]
so (25) and \(\mathrm{ass:below\mbox{-}elbow}\) give \(n\ell^d\le c_\ell^d\) for every \(n\ge2\).  Choose \(c_\ell>0\) sufficiently small to satisfy the series condition in (38).  Also
\[
n^2h^d\ell^da^2b^2
=c_a^2c_b^2n^2\ell^{2S+d+Sd/\gamma}
=c_a^2c_b^2c_\ell^{,2S+d+Sd/\gamma}, \tag{41}
\]
because \(\eta\{2+d/S+d/\gamma\}=2\).  Decrease the already fixed positive \(c_\ell\) once more so that the right side of (39) is at most \(1/4\).  This does not affect (27).  Finally, (28) gives the deterministic target separation
\[
|\tau_+(0)-\tau_-(0)|
=\frac{2ab}{p(1-p)}
=\frac{2c_ac_bc_\ell^S}{p(1-p)}n^{-\eta}
=c\rho_n,
\]
with \(c>0\).  All constants were chosen as functions only of the fixed parameter tuple.

For the requested early-kill tuple \(d=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/8\), \(\gamma=1\), one has \(S=1/4\), \(\eta=2/7\), \(\ell\asymp n^{-8/7}\), \(h\asymp n^{-2/7}\), and \(a=b\asymp n^{-1/7}\).  Thus \(n\ell\asymp n^{-1/7}\), singleton components vanish by (30), every \(r\ge2\) is included in (38), and \(n^2h\ell a^2b^2\asymp1\).  In particular, neither a singleton term nor a macro-scale leakage term survives.  This completes the certificate.
